summary: The patch fixes the crash by quoting table names, correctly resolving the reserved-word failure, but it hardcodes MySQL-style backticks instead of using Django's standard SQLite identifier quoting (quote_name / double quotes). It works functionally since SQLite accepts backticks, but is inconsistent with repo convention.

issues.description: Hardcoded backticks (`) for identifier quoting mismatch Django's SQLite convention. Elsewhere Django uses self.ops.quote_name(...) which emits double-quoted identifiers (SQL standard). Backticks are a MySQL-ism SQLite tolerates but idiomatic fix would call quote_name(table_name).

Column identifiers in the SELECT (primary_key_column_name, column_name) remain unquoted; a reserved-word column name would still fail. Out of the reported scope (table names) but the same class of bug is left partially unaddressed.
String-formatting identifiers via %s is fragile; relying on quote_name would be safer and self-documenting versus manually wrapping in literal backtick characters.
